description: IC-LoRA that restores natural colour to grayscale or desaturated footage, keeping subject, composition and motion. The monochrome clip is the reference video at 1x output size. Prompt in the trained dual-panel form: 'Reference shows ... Edited shows the same scene with natural colors restored. COLORIZE ... only color information differs.' A 0.9 preview weight trained at 960x544, 121 frames @ 24 fps; far above that size weakens it; lower toward 0.8 if it oversaturates
use_when: Colorize a black-and-white or washed-out clip

evidence.note: templates/ltx2/restore-colorize on lem (RTX 3090, uint4 SDNQ) at 960x544x121: natural colour on a greyscale street clip that the stored default prompt happens to describe, subject, framing and motion kept, 121 frames at the source's 24 fps; the colour holds only with a prompt matched to the clip - on an office-interview fixture the default and two generic prompts left it grey (1521f00bcf5a, 69e6bb12d56b, PSNR 36.7 dB to the source) and a prompt describing that clip and naming its colours coloured it (f80056a98e62, 49 frames, PSNR 30.2 dB); a portrait 384x544x97 run (c01a0fc6df48) came back at source size with no band or colour from the letterbox padding; 2.5 min including a cold load

Colour is reliable on a 24 fps 16:9 source and not on a low-frame-rate or portrait one, even with a clip-matched prompt (feature check, develop @ c69a6cbf, seed 1080): the 960x544 24 fps 121-frame office fixture coloured (718e232f76b0: warm skin, brown hair, blue lanyard); the same subject at 8 fps, 97 frames, stayed grey with frame_rate omitted (763968953985) and with frame_rate 24 (3579d7d376b2), and a 384x544 portrait crop, 97 frames, stayed grey (cf3ad9b05f4f) - each with only a faint blue lanyard, at the right rate, size and frame count, with no band or bleed. Cause not established (3x motion per frame at 8 fps; about 60% letterbox padding in the portrait's reference); check a frame of the result
